anatomy.flutter: Skeleton(width, height, radius) builds SizedBox > ClipRRect(borderRadius: radius ?? Radii.md) > KeyframePlayer > CustomPaint(_ShimmerPainter) drawing a repeating LinearGradient tile via LoadingShimmerMotion; a static Skeleton.span() factory returns a WidgetSpan(alignment: PlaceholderAlignment.middle) for inline placement.
anatomy.web: Skeleton({className, as: Tag = 'div', ...props}) renders one <Tag data-slot='skeleton' aria-hidden='true' className={cn('anim-shimmer rounded-md', Tag==='span' && 'inline-block', className)} /> — a single element whose geometry is entirely caller-supplied Tailwind classes.

api.flutter: Skeleton takes width/height/radius as explicit doubles (defaultRadius = Radii.md), with the caller expected to size every instance per the doc comment: 'The geometry is the caller's... a skeleton must match the footprint of what it replaces.'
api.web: Skeleton takes className and as: 'div'|'span', with sizing done entirely through Tailwind classes at each call site (h-32 w-full, size-8 rounded-pill, etc.), matching the same 'geometry is the caller's' philosophy the Flutter doc comment quotes from the reference.

states.flutter: Skeleton is a StatelessWidget with a single continuous shimmer animation and no rest/hover/focus/pressed/error state — it is itself a loading-state stand-in, not a control with its own state matrix.
states.web: skeleton.tsx defines no interactive states; it is a shimmering <div>/<span> with aria-hidden='true' and no hover/focus/press styling.
states.note: A skeleton IS the 'loading' state for whatever it replaces; it has no state matrix of its own on either platform, so the dimension does not apply.

disabled.flutter: Skeleton has no enabled/disabled field anywhere in skeleton.dart.
disabled.web: skeleton.tsx's Skeleton({className, as, ...props}) destructures no disabled prop and its class list carries no disabled: variant anywhere in the file.
disabled.note: A non-interactive placeholder has no operable state to disable on either side.

interaction.flutter: Skeleton wires no GestureDetector, Focus, or key handling; it is purely a CustomPaint animation.
interaction.web: skeleton.tsx renders a plain <div>/<span> with no onClick, tabIndex, or keyboard handling.
interaction.note: Neither implementation is operable by keyboard, pointer, or touch — a skeleton is decoration, not a control.

semantics.flutter: Skeleton's own doc comment records only that the *shape* is the caller's responsibility and says nothing about a Semantics/ExcludeSemantics wrapper; skeleton.dart's build() returns the SizedBox/ClipRRect/KeyframePlayer/CustomPaint tree with no Semantics node of any kind.
semantics.web: Skeleton always sets aria-hidden='true' on its host element, with an explicit comment: 'A shimmering rectangle has no text, so a screen reader reads it as an empty node... The state belongs to the CONTAINER (aria-busy, or a live region), which is what RULES §5 means... Overridable through the spread for the rare case where the placeholder is the only thing on the page.'
semantics.note: Reclassified on review from `gap`: the shortfall recorded below is on the FLUTTER side — the web has the capability, or Flutter's own doc comment records it as not ported, or Flutter reproduces an earlier state of the web source that has since moved on. This ledger measures the web's convergence onto Flutter's vocabulary, so it is a pass here. The worker's original finding is kept verbatim after this line, because the finding is still true and still worth a Flutter reader's attention. ORIGINAL: The web version explicitly hides every skeleton instance from assistive tech via aria-hidden='true' (overridable per-instance). Flutter's Skeleton emits no Semantics annotation at all, which means a screen reader traversing a Flutter tree containing a raw CustomPaint skeleton gets undefined behavior (most likely silently skipped since CustomPaint carries no semantic information by default) rather than the deliberate, documented aria-hidden choice the web makes — this is a real, if low-severity, documentation/parity gap since the Flutter side never states the equivalent choice.
